findings.claim: `SCORES=` set to an empty string is tested with `-n "${SCORES:-}"`, so it behaves like an unset SCORES. Nothing is marked and no message is printed. A caller who built the path from an empty variable (for example `SCORES="$dir/x.json"` with `$dir` unset gives a non-empty bad path and is caught, but `SCORES="$maybe_path"` with an empty value is not) gets silently unmarked controls. This is the same silent-degradation class as the F2 that this round fixed. The test suite and README do not cover the empty case.

Scored quotes whose run is not in RUNS, or whose id is not in the case arguments, are filtered out in jq without any message. This covers quotes for run 3 when RUNS="1 2". The same unattributed-quote class that F1 of the previous review fixed for a quote naming no finding remains for a quote whose run or case was not requested. A partial refreeze therefore reports no controls for those quotes without saying so. This is lower severity because a partial freeze may be intended.

`$runs` is expanded unquoted in both loops. A RUNS value containing glob characters (for example `RUNS='*'`) is expanded against the current directory's filenames before validation. The error message then names an arbitrary filename instead of `*`. The script has no `set -f`. This is a minor diagnostic defect on a developer-only tool. Ids from `"$@"` are matched against the `seen` list with space delimiters, so an id containing a space could collide with the next entry. Both are very unlikely inputs.
